**Final values:** a = 90, b = 36, TMP = 90.

**Approach.** Every addition is mod 100. Within each block, a variable's additions alternate between two amounts that sum to 100 (for example 22 and 78). Each such pair cancels, so an even number of additions has no net effect. An odd number leaves a net change equal to the first amount. TMP also gets some "+0" steps, which I skipped, and its non-zero additions are summed the same way. The program runs as 20 blocks, each starting with a reset of a or b.

| After block | a | b | TMP |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (a, b, TMP start at 6, 28, 61) | reset next | 6 | 6 |
| 2 (a ← 52) | reset next | 52 | 52 |
| 3 (a ← 30) | 52 | reset next | 30 |
| 4 (b ← 79) | reset next | 52 | 52 |
| 5 (a ← 46) | 52 | reset next | 46 |
| 6 (b ← 41) | 41 | reset next | 41 |
| 7 (b ← 17) | reset next | 41 | 17 |
| 8 (a ← 19) | 41 | reset next | 41 |
| 9 (b ← 78) | reset next | 41 | 78 |
| 10 (a ← 69) | 41 | reset next | 69 |
| 11 (b ← 39) | reset next | 41 | 39 |
| 12 (a ← 20) | 41 | reset next | 41 |
| 13 (b ← 12) | reset next | 41 | 12 |
| 14 (a ← 68) | 41 | reset next | 68 |
| 15 (b ← 42) | reset next | 41 | 41 |
| 16 (a ← 36) | reset next | 36 | 36 |
| 17 (a ← 35) | 36 | reset next | 35 |
| 18 (b ← 71) | reset next | 36 | 71 |
| 19 (a ← 98) | 36 | reset next | 36 |

**Block 20** starts with b ← 90, a = 36 and TMP = 36. It has 163 triples, with no reset afterwards.
- a gets 163 alternating additions of 54 and 46, starting with 54. That is an odd count, so the net is +54 and a = 36 + 54 = **90**.
- b gets 163 alternating additions of 46 and 54, starting with 46. The net is +46, so b = 90 + 46 = 136 mod 100 = **36**.
- TMP's non-zero additions strictly alternate 54, 46, …, starting and ending with 54. The net is +54, so TMP = 36 + 54 = **90**.

ANSWER: a ?= 90; b ?= 36; TMP ?= 90;
